startup.name: Mendelia
startup.one_liner: AI-powered back office employees for surgical practices
startup.description: Mendelia sells AI powered back office employees to surgical practices, meaning agents that take on administrative work such as scheduling, insurance authorization and billing follow up. The buyer is a surgical practice that pays a software or per task fee. Two founders in New York City, Winter 2026 batch. The description field is empty, so product depth, traction and the founders' backgrounds are unknown.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the Winter 2026 batch, so this is a note only. A random applicant starts near 1 percent. A concrete vertical, a paying buyer type and the healthcare AI theme would lift an application, but the empty description and unknown team background keep the number wide.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because AI agents for medical administration is one of the most crowded application categories, and the one line pitch does not show why two founders beat funded rivals. Reviewers would ask whether a founder has run a surgical practice, and how a narrow surgical niche reaches venture scale.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry Healthcare --calibration-only (seed 50 percent known only, range 46 to 54 percent, n=22, only 24 companies, anecdote); B2B 2022-2025 seed 59 percent, n=126; time table industry Healthcare months to seed median 19 (n=31, older batches).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 10.4 months, from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17. The 2022+ seed median is 6 months with a 75th percentile of 14 months, so roughly two thirds of eventual raisers are done by 10 months; Healthcare is slow to seed in the older data. I take about 0.65 to 0.7 of the 0.5 to 0.59 anchors, which is 0.35. Two founders and an AI agent theme do not lift it. The odds do not rank this company against others.

Institutional seed near the 2022+ seed median of $3.5M in the YC tables, which mixes in the YC deal so it reads low. Sized from the YC round size tables in references/tables/round_benchmarks.csv (2022+ rows) and public US medians from PitchBook and Carta.

Large seed led by a top fund, as press covered 2026 rounds in the winners test (median $6.0M among confirmed raises above $1M, a sample that leans high). Sized from the YC round size tables in references/tables/round_benchmarks.csv (2022+ rows) and public US medians from PitchBook and Carta.

Hot sector or pedigree round above $12M; rare, a small slice of the distribution. Sized from the YC round size tables in references/tables/round_benchmarks.csv (2022+ rows) and public US medians from PitchBook and Carta.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed fails if practices pilot but do not convert to paid annual contracts, since surgical practices are small buyers that move slowly and run on legacy systems. Many healthcare administration agent companies already exist, including Opencall and Novoflow from earlier YC batches, so investors compare traction directly. A narrow surgical niche may look too small, and Verse Therapy shows niche practice software ending in a small acquisition.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Ever anchor 0.25. A 10 month window is shorter than the 25th percentile of time to series A, so I use about an eighth of the anchor, 0.03. This is a window effect, not a verdict on the company.

bands.rationale: Thin A with a flat or small step up on modest recurring revenue. Sized from the YC round size tables in references/tables/round_benchmarks.csv (2022+ rows) and public US medians from PitchBook and Carta.

Typical 2022+ A: the YC table median is $15M and public deal size medians are $17M to $20M. Sized from the YC round size tables in references/tables/round_benchmarks.csv (2022+ rows) and public US medians from PitchBook and Carta.
Upside A after a breakout year, with a platform story. Sized from the YC round size tables in references/tables/round_benchmarks.csv (2022+ rows) and public US medians from PitchBook and Carta.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside 10 months is unlikely because it needs revenue across dozens of practices and an expansion story beyond surgery. Healthcare is slow to reach a Series A in the data, with a median of 29 months from the batch. Opencall and Decisional AI show agent companies that stayed small after the YC check.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B needs a platform across specialties with measurable revenue cycle savings and strong retention. If practices churn to the practice management vendors that add agents, growth stalls. Few healthcare administration analogs in the data have reached a B, the sample is small, and the Healthcare 2022-2025 cohort shows almost none so far, so there is little evidence that a surgical niche supports such a round.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C requires a large healthcare operations platform with enterprise contracts across specialties and regulatory certifications. Incumbent revenue cycle vendors and electronic health record companies sell the same workflows, and the analogs in the data rarely get this far, so the path is thin and slow.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most paths end in a stall or a small acquisition. A narrow surgical niche with two founders can become a modest software business, and Verse Therapy and Repool show small outcomes in practice and back office software. A full miss follows if practice management vendors bundle agents or if practices will not trust AI with insurance and billing work.

killers.mitigation: Win surgical specific workflows, such as surgical scheduling and implant authorization, with named practice references.

killers.risk: Small practices are slow, low budget buyers
killers.evidence: Verse Therapy and Opencall show practice software stays small without a large customer base.
killers.mitigation: Sell to surgical groups and ambulatory surgery centers, which have larger budgets.

killers.risk: Practice management and revenue cycle vendors add agents
killers.evidence: Established vendors such as Waystar sell automation for the same tasks.
killers.mitigation: Integrate with the incumbent systems and own the surgery workflow.

killers.risk: Trust and HIPAA concerns limit autonomy
killers.evidence: IDC notes prior authorization is exception heavy and unstructured, which hurts fully automated agents.
killers.mitigation: Keep human review for edge cases and publish accuracy metrics.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that drive payer portals, phone lines and practice management software are buildable in three months for narrow tasks, but accuracy, HIPAA controls and integrations with surgical scheduling and billing systems take much longer. Reliability on exception cases is the hard part.

takeover_risk.rationale: Funded agent vendors already serve medical practices, so adding a surgery workflow is a matter of months. Incumbent vendors have distribution into practices.

evidence.claim: Prior authorization and billing are costly administrative workflows that vendors and analysts say agentic AI can reduce.
Many vendors compete for the same practice back office budgets, which shows spend exists.

Integrate with two common surgical scheduling and billing systems.

actions: Hire an experienced healthcare operations seller.
roadmap.proof: Dozens of customers and net revenue retention above 110 percent.

brand.name: Mendelia
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score Mendelia --era 2022+ : kind suffix_coinage, alive 91.0 percent, n=133
strengths: Sounds like a medical science name, which suits healthcare buyers
weaknesses: Calls to mind Mendel and genetics, not surgery or back office work
brand.rationale: A suffix coinage with a science sound is typical for healthcare companies and shows no survival difference from other name types in the cohort. It may lend credibility with clinicians but it does not describe the product, and it will not decide the outcome.

narrative.headline: A plain vertical agent play in a crowded healthcare admin market, with a bit better than one in three chance of a seed inside 10 months.
narrative.general_summary: Mendelia sells AI staff to surgical practices. The need is real because practices spend on administrative labor, but the category is crowded with funded agent vendors and incumbents, and the description gives no traction or team background. The 10 month window is short, and Healthcare was slow to seed in older batches, so the seed estimate is discounted from the cohort anchor and does not rank this company against others. A Series A inside the window is very unlikely. Opencall and Novoflow show peers staying small.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-01-05, using the one liner, tags and team size only; the description field was empty.
Window is 10.4 months. Seed means a round above about $1M from outside investors closing inside the window; series_a given seed is for the same window.
Healthcare 2022-2025 cohort has only 24 companies, so B2B anchors are used too.
Founder backgrounds and traction are unknown.
